{{Short description|Pseudo-mathematician (1852–1937)}}
'''Carl Theodore Heisel''' (1852–1937)<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/21659237/carl-theodore-heisel |accessdate=31 May 2019|title=Carl Theodore Heisel (1852–1937)|website=[[Find a Grave]] }}</ref> was a mathematical  [[wikt:crank|crank]] who wrote several books in the 1930s challenging accepted mathematical truths. Among his claims is that he found a way to [[squaring the circle|square the circle]]. He is credited with 24 works in 62 publications.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.worldcat.org/identities/lccn-no2002070146/ |accessdate=16 May 2019 |title=WorldCat Listing}}</ref> Heisel did not charge money for his books; he gave thousands of them away for free. Because of this, they are available at many libraries and universities. Heisel's books have historic and monetary value.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Simanek |first1=Donald E. |title=Carl Theodore Heisel Squares the Circle |url=https://lockhaven.edu/~dsimanek/pseudo/heisel.htm |website=lockhaven.edu |accessdate=23 May 2019 |archive-date=26 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210226183023/https://www.lockhaven.edu/~dsimanek/pseudo/heisel.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> [[Paul Halmos]] referred to one of Heisel's works (a book claiming to have accomplished the impossible task of [[squaring the circle]]) as a "classic crank book."<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://www.e-periodica.ch/digbib/view?pid=ens-001%3A1970%3A16%3A%3A524#278 | author=Paul R. Halmos | title=How to Write Mathematics | journal=[[L'Enseignement mathématique]] | volume=16 | number=2 | pages=123–152 | year=1970 }} – [https://entropiesschool.sciencesconf.org/data/How_to_Write_Mathematics.pdf How to Write Mathematics]</ref>
